idea: Hold TQQQ only inside hardcoded scheduled FOMC post-decision and monthly OpEx windows, BIL otherwise.
hypothesis: The FOMC-cycle (post-decision even-week) premium and the monthly OpEx flow week are concentrated calendar returns; a 3x Nasdaq fund captures them without bearing the odd-week drawdown.

calendar.note: 2024-2026 dates are ex-ante schedule dates, included in the hardcoded lists, but no 2024+ bar enters the panel, weights or simulation of this development run.

dev_only_calendar_replay.note: the 2024-2026 calendar entries are inert in the dev window; adding them does not change the 2016-2023 result.

G7.note: G3 + soft vol gate (x0.5 above q75)

G8.note: G3 + hard vol gate (0 above q75)

event_study.note: per-event open-to-open return, same number and lengths as the primary; random null 4,000 draws

exposure_arithmetic.note: raw TQQQ open-to-open return of the held blocks, before BIL yield and costs.  If this CAGR is below 36.72%, no cash/cost treatment of the same calendar can clear the bar.

shift_test.note: every FOMC and OpEx anchor shifted by N sessions; same window lengths, no gate.  A genuine calendar effect should peak at 0.

placebo.note: Random session starts with the same number and lengths of FOMC and OpEx windows.  'unmatched' preserves window structure but random placement overlaps more, so its exposure is lower.  'matched' adds/removes random sessions to hold exactly the primary's number of sessions and is the headline placebo: it asks whether the calendar timing adds anything beyond the same TQQQ exposure.
placebo.matched_note: exactly exposure-matched to the primary's held session count

verdict: FAIL at the development bar: G3 30.60% CAGR vs 36.72% (-6.12 pp), max DD 51.70% vs 82.29%, Sharpe 0.80. TQQQ exposure 58.1%. Best grid cell G6 at 45.05%.
notes: The 2024-2026 calendar dates are hardcoded and ex-ante; the development panel is truncated at 2023-12-29 and the full-vs-dev weight difference is exactly 0.0.
The benchmark is recomputed on the same 1-minute panel; the published 36.72% / 82.29% / 0.82 bar is used for pass/fail.
TQQQ exposure is the mean TQQQ weight over 1-minute bars, not bt.stats' exposure (which includes the BIL leg).
The primary is pure calendar G3; G7/G8 are pre-registered risk variants and are not selection candidates.

precut_test.note: weights strictly before 2020-03-12 11:07 rebuilt on a panel truncated at the cut; the calendar-only primary should be exact.
